title: PromptBox settings popup: a read-only LoRA rack at the top - name badge, strength, bypass

summary: Carded from Fabio's request: the PromptBox cog popup names no LoRAs. Brief + plan written. The rack is READ-ONLY by design - MPI-356 stripped the popup to parameters only, so it picks no file and adds no slot; it lists filled slots with the two knobs that belong to each (strength, bypass) and reads None when the model has none. Reuses project.modelSettings[modelId].loras in MpiModelSettings' exact write shape (settings:model:update, key 'loras', no opName) - no schema, engine or injector work. BLOCKED on MPI-721, which owns MpiPromptBox.js and .css. Open question for Fabio recorded in plan.md: whether MpiModelSettings' six fixed slots should also collapse to filled-only.

Fabio settled the three open points, brief + plan rewritten. (1) Empty state is NOTHING - no label, no rows, no placeholder; the earlier 'None' reading is dead. (2) The section carries a LORAS label, and for a staged model (Wan, models.js:1297) the stage's own label + ' LORAS' replaces it, HIGH NOISE then LOW NOISE, a stage with no filled slot rendering nothing. (3) NEW requirement: two-way LIVE sync with MpiModelSettings, both directions, not just on reopen - both surfaces listen to settings:model:update filtered on key 'loras' and skip their own echo with a _selfWrite flag (Events.emit is synchronous, events.js:59). That forces buildStrengthsRow to return its MpiInput handles so sync can setValue in place instead of rebuilding, which would tear down an open TreePicker or steal focus mid-type. MpiModelSettings' six fixed slots stay - it is the only place a LoRA can be added. Still BLOCKED on MPI-721 (owns MpiPromptBox.js and .css).

Fabio confirmed the two open calls. Stage order is HIGH NOISE then LOW NOISE in the prompt box, matching models.js:1297 and the overlay - he said 'low and high' in speech but corrected it to high first. And the rack can NEVER change the set: no picker, no +, no clear, no empty slot; adding and removing stays in MpiModelSettings, the prompt box only adjusts strengths and bypasses. Written into plan.md Scope as a settled non-goal rather than an inference. Blocker lifted in the same pass: MPI-721 closed at 02:51 and its write claim on MpiPromptBox.js/.css (state/files/f2c79865) reads status complete, so the card is ready to pick up - but § Current State line numbers predate MPI-721's media-strip rewrite and must be re-read at claim time.

reason: Fabio said start. MPI-721 closed so MpiPromptBox.js and .css are free.

Shipped and measured: lint clean, 921 tests, 20 live checks in an isolated instance incl. two-way sync and a debounce regression found and fixed. One human call left - does it look right in the popup.
Fabio verified it in his own app: 'yeah, it's looking good.' Badge de-pilled and height-matched in the same pass.

summary: Closed. Fabio's look found the one thing the measurements could not: the name badge read as a different family of control - too rounded, and shorter than the row. Both were one prop. .mpi-badge is already border-radius --r-2, the same 4px the row, the strength fields and the bypass button use, so pill:true was the entire roundness and neither a new badge variant nor a replacement control was needed. Dropped it, stretched the name cell (the row is align-items:center, which left the badge at content height) and left-aligned the label: measured 26px badge / 26px bypass / 25.6px field, radius 4px. Fabio confirmed in his own app on Krea 2. File claim c7a41d05 released.

Close-out finished (b226129c). Fabio approved both proposals: MpiLoraRack is now in component-mounts.md under MpiPromptBox's internal mounts and has its own entry in component-events-primitives.md, where MpiModelSettings' 'LISTENS: none' was also wrong and is corrected. UNRELEASED.md gains a What's new entry. The claim auditor earned its keep: 9103098a claims to mount the rack in the popup, but those MpiPromptBox.js hunks are in 4f493f4f, a peer's MPI-677 commit 34s earlier - git apply --cached staged them into the index, which is ONE file shared by every session, and the peer committed first. Nothing broken: the three commits together are the reviewed change and HEAD matches what was verified, so the attribution is recorded in validation.md rather than rewritten. Both file claims released.
